scgsim-kind: "course"

Continue in the session from [shared Xmon inputs](../tutorial-xmon-input.qmd),
with `snapshot` prepared. Before asking a backend to build geometry, inspect
what you actually supplied. A missing Net, wrong material interval or unintended
vacuum envelope is easier to understand at the source boundary.

```python
from IPython.display import display
from scgsim.sgb import summarize_geometry_input

summary = summarize_geometry_input(
    snapshot.geometry_input, prepared_stack=snapshot.stack
)
display(summary)
source_data = summary.data
```

Read the Entity/occurrence/Net table against your final assignment, then the
material, Z and vacuum records. The port table identifies the authored sheet
and its host/direction. Unknown values remain unknown; an unset request is not
the same as a known zero. `.data` is detached, so editing the returned dictionary
does not change the retained source snapshot.

Both Eigenmode facades also offer `sim.input_summary()` after configuration.
That view adds the backend settings to the normalized source. Electrostatic has
no such facade method: use the standalone source summary above, then inspect
its written config and exact terminal/ground index.

## Retain a portable paired source

The snapshot has no live component references. Its GDS bytes and detached stack
form a portable pair, allowing a later session to read the same source without
reconstructing the coupon in a live GDSFactory cache.

```python
import json
from pathlib import Path
from scgsim.sgb import build_gds_stack_geometry_input

source_dir = Path(".artifacts/public-xmon-source")
source_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
gds_path = source_dir / "xmon.gds"
stack_path = source_dir / "xmon.stack.json"
gds_path.write_bytes(snapshot.gds_bytes)
stack_path.write_text(json.dumps(snapshot.stack, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
reloaded = build_gds_stack_geometry_input(
    gds_file=gds_path,
    stack_file=stack_path,
    top_cell_name=snapshot.stack["metadata"]["top_cell_name"],
)
print(snapshot.gds_sha256)
print(tuple(entity.semantic_id for entity in reloaded.entities))
```

Choose your own new study location when preserving an earlier pair. Keep the
pair together: the stack reader checks the recorded GDS identity and registered
occurrence geometry. The printed Entity IDs are source lineage. They do not
establish one field measurement per Entity or solver connectivity.

A source summary and paired-source read establish normalized input facts.
They do not mesh, query native AEDT, or demonstrate a solve. The next stage
chooses a physical model:
[Palace Electrostatic](palace-electrostatic.qmd),
[Palace Eigenmode](palace-eigenmode.qmd), or
[AEDT source-first Eigenmode/EPR](../tutorial-xmon-aedt.qmd).
The [geometry concept](../concepts/geometry.qmd) explains why those backends can
share source identity while using different native representations.
